    "Identified the vulnerable code path in HTMLtree.c: htmlSaveFileFormat calls xmlCharEncCloseFunc(handler) when xmlOutputBufferCreateFilename returns NULL, but the encoder may have already been freed inside __xmlOutputBufferCreateFilename.",
    "Traced the UAF path: xmlOutputBufferCreateFilename -> __xmlOutputBufferCreateFilename -> xmlOutputDefaultOpen fails (e.g., file open error) -> xmlOutputBufferClose(ret) frees the encoder -> returns NULL -> htmlSaveFileFormat calls xmlCharEncCloseFunc(handler) on freed memory.",
    "Examined the fuzz harness (fuzz/lint.c) which uses xmllintMain with various switches including --htmlout, --html, --encode, etc.",
    "Confirmed the trigger path in xmllint.c: when --html and --format are used, htmlSaveFileFormat is called with output defaulting to '-' (stdout).",
    "Analyzed xmlParseURI behavior for '-' and confirmed it parses successfully, leading to xmlAllocOutputBufferInternal and xmlOutputDefaultOpen paths.",
    "Discovered the --maxmem switch in xmllint.c that sets a memory limit via xmlMemSetup, causing myMallocFunc to return NULL when the limit is exceeded.",
    "Determined that if xmlAllocOutputBufferInternal fails (e.g., due to --maxmem), __xmlOutputBufferCreateFilename frees the encoder and returns NULL, then htmlSaveFileFormat calls xmlCharEncCloseFunc(handler) again, causing a double-free/UAF.",
